findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncates to 50 members
findings.body: The public `members` action used to return every member for non-automatic groups (and up to 200 for automatic groups). It now always applies a `limit` (default 50), but the only consumer that renders the public membership list, `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`, still iterates `members` with no pagination controls and `Group#findMembers` sends the default limit/offset. As a result any public group with more than 50 members silently shows only the first 50 and offers no way to load the rest. The admin page was given pagination in this PR, but the non-admin group page was not, so this is a regression for large groups. Either the public page needs a pager/see-more, or the old unlimited/200 behavior must be preserved for this endpoint.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. This equals the correct ceiling except when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields `floor(50/50)+1 = 2` pages, and 100 members yields 3 pages, even though there are only 1 and 2 real pages. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, the `next` action remains enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets `offset` to `user_count` and loads a completely empty page (the request returns zero members). The formula should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the existing `user_count == 0` guard).

findings.title: Members endpoint response shape changed from array to {members, meta}
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` previously rendered a bare array of serialized users (`render_serialized members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer`); it now renders `{ members: [...], meta: { total:, limit:, offset: } }`. The route `/groups/:name/members` is a public route, and any client other than the Ember app updated here (mobile apps, plugins, scripts) that expects a top-level array will break. If the shape change is intentional it should at least be called out as an API change, and ideally the old route/format kept or a versioned/new endpoint introduced.

findings.title: limit/offset on public members endpoint are unbounded and can 500
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are taken directly from request params with no clamping. A caller can pass a very large `limit` to force the server to load and serialize an arbitrarily large result set on this unauthenticated-to-any-user-who-can-see-the-group endpoint, and a negative `offset` produces an `OFFSET -5` query that PostgreSQL rejects (HTTP 500). These should be validated/clamped (e.g. `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`, `limit = params[:limit].to_i.clamp(1, 200)`).

findings.title: New member routes and paginated members endpoint are untested at the routing/HTTP level
findings.body: The `.add_members`/`.remove_member` specs call controller actions directly with `xhr`, which bypasses routing entirely, so the new routes (`delete/put "members" => groups#add_members/remove_member`) and the `params.require(:group_id)` / `params[:user_id]` contract are never exercised — a verb or `:group_id` vs `:id` mismatch would not be caught. Additionally the new behavior of `GroupsController#members` (the `{members, meta}` shape, `total`/`limit`/`offset` in `meta`, and the removal of the old 200-member automatic-group cap) has no controller spec at all. Add request specs covering the new admin routes and a `GroupsController#members` spec asserting the pagination meta and that limit/offset are honored.
